name: Ironpass HullWork Synth Labor Coverall
description: Heavy-duty graphite canvas coverall pre-tailored in seven modular torso lengths and four limb-extension kits, sold as a configured bundle at point of assignment. Reinforced knee and elbow panels are replaceable via rivet-press without removing the garment. Hi-vis yellow chevrons run the chest and back, and every seam is double-welded for chemical splash resistance. No branding beyond a stamped lot number — this is infrastructure clothing.
functionality: Modular torso/limb length configuration, field-replaceable reinforcement panels, chemical splash resistance.
what_it_says: This body works, gets damaged, and keeps working.
story_hooks: Lot number 7-DELTA-9 was recalled — the canvas leaches a compound that interferes with synthetic cognition after prolonged wear.
A labor unit has been secretly marking shift counts inside the collar — 1,847 days with no rotation.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body coverall with a boxy, industrial silhouette. The garment reads as pure function—no aesthetic concession. Broad shoulders, straight torso, and tapered ankles create a uniform column of graphite gray punctuated by safety yellow. Worn primarily by Tier 3 and Tier 4 machine operators, maintenance crews, and industrial workers across the GLMZ.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, deliberate. Cut for layering over undergarments and light augmentation hardware. The modular torso allows custom length configuration; limb-extension kits accommodate both natural and synthetic limbs. Armholes are generous for prosthetic shoulders. Ankle cuffs are adjustable via friction-lock.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy graphite-toned canvas—a ballistic-weave synthetic blend rated for chemical splash and thermal stress. The material is matte, industrial-grade, with no sheen. Designed for durability over 2,000+ operating hours per configuration.
physical_description.texture: Coarse, rigid when new; softens with use into a broken-in suppleness. The double-welded seams create subtle ridge lines that catch light. Replaceable knee and elbow panels are riveted, creating small raised circles of texture against the flat base fabric.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant graphite gray (70%), with hi-vis safety yellow chevrons running full-width across the chest and mirrored on the back. No additional branding or pattern—the yellow is the only visual accent.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snap front placket (military-grade, rated for repeated use). Wrist cuffs and ankle cuffs close via friction-lock cinch bands. No conventional zippers—all seams are sealed.
distinctive_features: Replaceable rivet-press knee and elbow panels
Modular torso length configuration (seven lengths per assignment)
Interchangeable limb-extension kits for prosthetic accommodation
Double-welded seams throughout for chemical resistance
Stamped lot number only (no corporate branding)
Integrated tool-loop rings on hips and thighs
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 working class. This is assignment clothing—issued, not purchased. Signals stable industrial employment and corpo-adjacent infrastructure work.
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of GLMZ machine operators, maintenance technicians, chemical processors, and autonomous Iowan Behemoth handlers. Wearing this says: *I am infrastructure. I work with my hands and augmentations. I follow assignments.* It is seen in factories, refineries, water treatment plants, and the lower levels of corpo arcologies. No street cred—pure utilitarian.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn but maintained. Minor stains from solvents and grease. Knee and elbow panels are often visibly patched or recently replaced. Seams remain intact. The graphite canvas develops a lighter sheen on high-friction areas (hips, shoulders). Never pristine; always working.
